About CaspianTools
One platform, because
the work is one thing

Organizations do not experience themselves as eleven departments. People do the work,
        equipment supports it, money follows it and safety governs all of it. The software
        should reflect that.
Why we built it

Field operations end up with a familiar sprawl: an HR system nobody likes, safety in
          spreadsheets, procurement in an inbox, maintenance in a whiteboard photo, and finance
          reconciling all of it a month later.

Every one of those tools is defensible on its own. Together they create the real cost:
          the same person entered four times, a competency that expired without anyone noticing,
          a purchase order nobody can match to a receipt, and a monthly report that takes a week
          to assemble and is out of date the day it lands.

Caspian ERP was built the other way round — one multi-tenant platform where the modules
          share people, items, documents, permissions and reporting from the start. Not an
          integration project. One system.

More questions on the pricing page
Do we have to adopt all eleven modules?

No. Every department and every individual tool can be switched on or off in Settings. Most teams start with one or two — usually HSEQ or Efficiency — and turn on the rest as they go. The sidebar, search and permissions all follow the switches.
How long does it take to get running?
Account setup is only the first step. A working rollout also needs data preparation, roles, configuration and training. Start with one workflow and agree a schedule based on your team and data.
Can we bring existing data in?

Yes. The main lists support CSV import and export, so personnel, items, vendors and assets can be loaded from your current spreadsheets or exports. For large or unusual migrations, talk to us before you start.
Who can see what?

Access is permission-based. Each tool has its own read / create / update / delete permissions, roles are collections of those permissions, and every member holds exactly one role in each organization. The rules are enforced server-side, so a permission you did not grant cannot be reached by any client.
Does it work on phones and tablets in the field?
Caspian ERP runs in the browser on desktop, tablet and phone — there is no app to install or update. Field capture such as observations, checklists and attendance is built for small screens.
What happens to our data if we leave?
It stays yours. Lists export to CSV at any time, and we will provide a full export of your organization's records on request before an account is closed.

Administration questions we get asked
Can we really turn off modules we do not use?

Yes — whole departments or single tools, at any time. The sidebar, the global search and the permission registry all follow the switches, so people are not navigating past features that do not apply to them.
What happens to the data if we switch a module off?
It stays. Switching a module off hides it from the interface; turning it back on later brings it back with its records intact.
How specific can a custom role be?

Down to read, create, update and delete on an individual tool. That is enough to build a role that matches a real job — a permit issuer who can sign but not configure, a storekeeper who can issue stock but not adjust it.
Is hiding a tool the same as securing it?
No, and we do not treat it that way. Permissions are enforced by server-side security rules, so a permission you did not grant cannot be reached by any client regardless of what the interface shows.
Do we need a consultant to set this up?

No. Creating the organization, choosing modules, defining roles and inviting people is a settings exercise an administrator does directly. If you want help with a large migration, ask us — but the configuration itself is yours.
Can one company run several organizations?
Yes. Groups, joint ventures and consultancies commonly do. One account can belong to several organizations and switch between them, and data never crosses the boundary between them.

Can permits to work be raised and closed in the field?

Inventory questions we get asked
Can we run several warehouses and site stores?
Yes. Stock is held per item per location, so a main store, a yard and a container on site are separate records with their own minimum levels — not one blended number.
Do we have to stop work to count?
No, that is the point of cycle counting. You define plans for what gets counted and how often, and counts are performed in the aisle on a phone while the warehouse keeps operating.
How does stock stay accurate?

Because the actions that do the work are the actions that move the stock. A goods receipt in Procurement, an issue to a maintenance work order and a transfer between sites each create a movement, so accuracy does not depend on someone remembering to update a second system.
Can we trace a batch back to its supplier?
For lot-tracked items, yes. Inventory lots record the batch from receipt onwards, so you can trace where a given lot went and which order it arrived on.
Does inventory value flow into finance?
Movements and adjustments are recorded with reasons and attribution, which is what a valuation needs. Finance works from the same item catalogue, so codes agree across the two.

Is this a telematics or GPS tracking system?

No. It is the management layer around journeys — planning, risk, approval and check-ins — plus the vehicle register and its documents. It does not replace a tracker fitted to a vehicle, and does not pretend to.

What happens when a check-in is missed?

Stock leaves the sending location on dispatch and is visible as in transit until the receiving location confirms it. That in-between state is exactly what a phone call loses.

Procurement questions we get asked
Does a goods receipt update stock automatically?
Yes. The receipt is the stock movement — procurement and inventory share the same item catalogue and the same warehouse records, so there is no second entry and no reconciliation between the two.
Can we enforce that invoices are matched before payment?
Yes. Three-way matching between the purchase order, the goods receipt and the vendor invoice is a configurable requirement. Your administrator decides how strict it is.
How are contractor personnel different from employees?

They belong to a vendor rather than to your payroll, and they are recorded in Procurement for that reason. Everything else is the same: certificates, validity dates and competence checks before they are allowed on a job.
Where do vendor scorecards come from?
From the delivery and quality history already recorded against that vendor’s orders and receipts. They are not a separate survey someone has to fill in.
Can we import our supplier list and item catalogue?
Yes, both support CSV import and export. Agreeing your item categories before the first import saves rework later, since the catalogue is shared with inventory, manufacturing and finance.

Security & access control — Caspian ERP
Multi-tenant isolation, permission-based RBAC enforced server-side, verified invitations and an audit log. How Caspian ERP protects your organization's data.
Security & access control
Permissions enforced
in the database

An ERP holds your incidents, your medical records, your salaries and your contracts.
        Hiding a menu item is not access control — so in Caspian ERP every read and write is
        checked server-side against the permissions you granted.
Tenant isolation
Every record lives under its organization and carries its organization's ID. A query that reaches outside your organization is rejected by the rules, not filtered by the client.
Permission-based RBAC
Each tool has its own read, create, update and delete permissions. A role is a set of permissions; a member holds one role per organization. Nothing is implied by job title.
Membership, role and permission changes are written to an append-only log attributed to the member who made them — entries cannot be forged in another member's name.
Verified invitations
An invitation can only be discovered and accepted by a verified email address, so nobody joins your organization by registering someone else's address.
Least privilege by default
Ownership, billing plan and member quota are platform-owned fields — an administrator cannot promote themselves to owner or change your plan from inside the app.
Hardened transport
HTTPS everywhere, security headers, a content security policy, and per-user rate limits on every server route.
How access is decided

Four questions are answered on the server for every single operation. If any answer
          is no, the operation fails — whatever the browser thinks.
Are you signed in?
Authentication via Google or email and password, with email verification required for password accounts.
Are you an active member of this organization?
Suspended and offboarded members lose access immediately; suspended organizations become read-only.
Does your role hold this permission?
Checked per tool and per action — read, create, update or delete — against the permission registry.
Does the record belong to your organization?
Enforced on the document path and its organization ID, on reads and on writes alike.

Common security questions
Where is our data stored?

In Google Cloud, in a managed database dedicated to the platform, with your records namespaced under your organization. If your business has a specific data-residency requirement, raise it with us before you sign — we will tell you plainly whether we can meet it.
Can one customer see another customer's data?

No. Every document sits beneath its organization and carries its organization ID, and the security rules check both membership and permission on every read and write. There is no client-side filter you could bypass.
How do we remove someone who has left?
Suspend or offboard their membership in Settings → Team. Access ends immediately, their historical records stay intact and attributed, and the change is recorded in the audit log.

Google sign-in is supported today alongside email and password with verification. If you need SAML or another identity provider, tell us — it is on the roadmap and customer demand is what orders it.
